tool.name: nf-core jupyternotebook
tool.description: Render jupyter (or jupytext) notebooks to HTML reports. Supports parametrization through papermill.
tool.command:
<![CDATA[ set -o pipefail
# write .params.yml file if required $params_cmd
# Create output directory mkdir artifacts
# Set parallelism for BLAS/MKL etc. to avoid over-booking of resources export MKL_NUM_THREADS="$task.cpus" export OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS="$task.cpus" export OMP_NUM_THREADS="$task.cpus" export NUMBA_NUM_THREADS="$task.cpus"
# Set temporary directory to remove warning about Matplotlib creating temporary directory export MPLCONFIGDIR=./tmp
# Convert notebook to ipynb using jupytext, execute using papermill, convert using nbconvert jupytext --to notebook --output - --set-kernel ${kernel} ${notebook} > ${notebook}.ipynb ${render_cmd} ${notebook}.ipynb ${notebook}.executed.ipynb jupyter nbconvert --stdin --to html --output ${prefix}.html < ${notebook}.executed.ipynb
cat <<-END_VERSIONS > versions.yml "${task.process}": jupytext: \$(jupytext --version) ipykernel: \$(python -c "import ipykernel; print(ipykernel.__version__)") nbconvert: \$(jupyter nbconvert --version) papermill: \$(papermill --version | cut -f1 -d' ') END_VERSIONS ]]>
tool.help:
<![CDATA[ **What it does**
Render jupyter (or jupytext) notebooks to HTML reports. Supports parametrization through papermill.

For more information about this tool, visit: https://github.com/nf-core/modules/tree/master/modules/nf-core/jupyternotebook ]]>
